Published online:
    September 4, 2026

Geographic focus:
    Global (primary focus: Japan, USA; secondary: New Zealand, Australia, Middle East)

Temporal focus:
    T1. Historical report [YES]
    T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
    T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

Synopsis:
    The yen posted its strongest weekly gain since late July, driven by rising BOJ rate hike expectations ahead of the Sept 17-18 meeting, despite intraday pullback. The dollar softened modestly ahead of NFP and CPI data critical to the Fed's Sept 15-16 decision. Fed Governor Waller signaled a hold if inflation continues moderating, pulling September hike odds back to 50/50. JPMorgan flagged yen short-squeeze risk (142-146 range). Oil remains elevated above $95 on US-Iran tensions. Bitcoin up ~3% on the week on debasement fears.

Q01. Is the content relevant to US economy, US yields, US interest rates and US market pricing?
Relevance: YES

Q02. Is the content about increasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 45 (moderately relevant — September hike is still live at 50% implied probability, but momentum is fading)
Increasing rates magnitude: 0.25% (standard 25bps increment implied by market pricing)

Q03. Is the content about holding stable US interest rates?
Relevance: 55 (Waller's comments lean toward a hold contingent on incoming inflation data, pulling the narrative toward pause)

Q04. Is the content about decreasing US interest rates?
Relevance: 5 (no material discussion of cuts)
Decreasing rates magnitude: N/A

Q05. Focus on the very latest information: Is it striking a different sentiment/tone compared to previous discussions on US interest rates?
Difference: -30 (More dovish than before — Waller's conditional hold guidance and the paring of September hike bets represent a notable dovish tilt relative to prior hawkish framing)

Q06. Focus on the very latest information: How does it compare to previous information on US interest rates?
Difference: -30 (The implied probability of a September hike retreating to 50% and a senior Fed governor explicitly leaning toward holding marks a clear dovish shift vs. earlier expectations that had been pricing a more aggressive path)
